boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Northern Iowa
boards.description: Ten currently documented Cedar Falls food stops with late evening or overnight availability; confirm hours before heading out.

cards.title: Taco Bell on University Avenue
cards.subtitle: 6023 University Avenue, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need a late option; the location lists overnight service every day, with later closing on Thursday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A University Avenue stop with the latest documented hours in Cedar Falls.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours until 4 AM Sunday through Wednesday and 5 AM Thursday through Saturday at 6023 University Avenue.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 6023 University Avenue, Cedar Falls
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is listed until 4 AM Sunday–Wednesday and 5 AM Thursday–Saturday; dine-in hours differ.

cards.title: Domino's on College Street
cards.subtitle: 2024 College Street, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Place a carryout or delivery order before leaving; the official location page currently shows this College Street store open until 2 AM.
cards.short_summary: A College Street pizza option with documented 2 AM availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's lists its 2024 College Street Cedar Falls location as open until 2 AM.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza at 2024 College St. — Cedar Falls
cards.access_notes: The official store page currently displays “Open Today Until 2:00 AM”; check the ordering page for day-specific availability.

cards.title: Papa Johns on West 1st
cards.subtitle: 1322 W 1st St, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Choose delivery or carryout and check the day first; delivery runs later than carryout on Friday and Saturday at this West 1st Street store.
cards.short_summary: Pizza delivery listed until 2 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists delivery until 2 AM Friday and Saturday and carryout until 1:30 AM at 1322 W 1st St.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Pizza W 1st St — Cedar Falls
cards.access_notes: Delivery is listed until 2 AM Friday–Saturday; carryout is listed until 1:30 AM those nights and midnight other days.

cards.title: Tony's LaPizzeria
cards.subtitle: 407 Main Street, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Plan this for Friday or Saturday and confirm before going; the downtown district lists 2 AM closing on both nights for this pizza restaurant.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pizza counter with Friday and Saturday 2 AM hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Cedar Falls Downtown District lists Tony's LaPizzeria open until 2 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Cedar Falls Downtown District — Tony's LaPizzeria
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Friday 4 PM–2 AM and Saturday 11:30 AM–2 AM; closed Monday and Tuesday.

cards.title: Pancheros on University Avenue
cards.subtitle: 6421 University Avenue, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Use the University Avenue store for a late burrito, bowl, taco, salad, or quesadilla; its official location page posts midnight and 2 AM closing times.
cards.short_summary: A burrito stop with midnight hours most nights and 2 AM late-week service.
cards.evidence_claim: Pancheros lists its Cedar Falls location open until midnight Sunday through Wednesday and until 2 AM Thursday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Store hours are listed as 10:30 AM–midnight Sunday–Wednesday and 10:30 AM–2 AM Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on University Avenue
cards.subtitle: 6719 University Ave, Suite 3, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Order delivery or carryout from this University Avenue shop; the official location listing shows midnight closing most days and 1 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A late University Avenue pizza option with 1 AM weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut lists restaurant hours until midnight Monday through Thursday and until 1 AM Friday and Saturday at 6719 University Ave.
cards.source_title: Pizza Hut — 6719 University Ave, Cedar Falls
cards.access_notes: The official page lists 9 AM–midnight Monday–Thursday and 9 AM–1 AM Friday–Saturday; verify Sunday hours when ordering.

cards.title: Raising Cane's at Viking Plaza
cards.subtitle: 201 Viking Plaza Drive, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Pick drive-thru, curbside, or dine-in at the Viking Plaza location; it posts midnight closing Sunday through Thursday and 1 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.short_summary: Chicken-finger meals with a documented midnight-or-later schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's lists its 201 Viking Plaza Drive restaurant open until midnight Sunday through Thursday and 1 AM Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's — Vikings Plaza Dr, Cedar Falls
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru and dine-in are both listed until midnight Sunday–Thursday and 1 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Zurys Taco Bar
cards.subtitle: 2214 College St, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Make Wednesday the late option here: the restaurant's own hours list service until midnight, while Thursday through Saturday close at 11 PM.
cards.short_summary: A College Street taco restaurant with a documented Wednesday midnight close.
cards.evidence_claim: Zurys Taco Bar lists Wednesday hours of 11 AM to midnight at 2214 College St.
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours list Wednesday until midnight, Thursday–Saturday until 11 PM, and earlier closes Sunday–Tuesday.

cards.title: Mulligans Brick Oven Grill
cards.subtitle: Cedar Falls, near 18th Street and Cedar Prairie Trail
cards.notes: Use the restaurant's food and carryout offerings for a late meal; its official page lists midnight closing Thursday through Saturday and carryout ordering.
cards.short_summary: Brick-oven pizza and food with a documented midnight weekend close.
cards.evidence_claim: Mulligans lists hours until midnight Thursday through Saturday and offers carryout ordering.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are 11 AM–11 PM Sunday–Wednesday and 11 AM–midnight Thursday–Saturday; carryout is available.

cards.title: Casey's on University Avenue
cards.subtitle: 5226 University Ave, Cedar Falls
cards.notes: Use this convenience-store stop for pizza, sandwiches, wings, bakery items, or snacks; the store is listed open until 11 PM, with pickup until 10:30 PM.
cards.short_summary: A late convenience and prepared-food option on University Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Casey's lists its 5226 University Ave Cedar Falls store open daily from 5 AM to 11 PM, with pickup until 10:30 PM.
cards.access_notes: Store hours are listed daily until 11 PM; pickup and delivery are listed daily until 10:30 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UNI spaces for collaboration, focused study, creative work, campus events, and gathering.

cards.title: Book a Rod Library Study Room
cards.subtitle: Rod Library · individual or small-group work
cards.notes: Reserve a room for one to six people when your project needs a table, monitor, whiteboard, and a defined place to work together.
cards.short_summary: Reservable small-group and individual study rooms in the center-of-campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library lists study rooms for one to six people as individual or small-group spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s room-reservation link; availability varies.

cards.title: Use the Learning Commons for Collaboration
cards.subtitle: Rod Library main floor · high-sound floor
cards.notes: Choose the main-floor Learning Commons for a conversation-friendly study session, then move to a quieter floor when you need less sound.
cards.short_summary: Rod Library’s main-floor collaborative study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library identifies its main floor as a High Sound floor intended to encourage collaboration in studying and learning.
cards.access_notes: The library’s floor sound designations guide where collaborative work fits.

cards.title: Make Something at the Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Rod Library · creative work space
cards.notes: Bring a class idea or a small creative project and check the library’s Makerspace information before you go for current tools and access details.
cards.short_summary: A named Rod Library space for hands-on creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library lists Makerspace among its popular spaces to unwind and depicts students building there.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current Makerspace guidance before planning a visit.

cards.title: Take a Reset in the Mindfulness Space
cards.subtitle: Rod Library · quiet reset space
cards.notes: Build in a short reset between classes or study blocks by locating the library’s Mindfulness Space and following any posted room guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named Rod Library space set apart from regular study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library lists a Mindfulness Space among its popular spaces to unwind.
cards.access_notes: Consult library information or signage for current use expectations.

cards.title: Study Models in the Anatomy Room
cards.subtitle: Rod Library main floor · LIB 280
cards.notes: If anatomy is on your schedule, use LIB 280’s SynDaver and muscle model as a focused supplement to course materials and lab study.
cards.short_summary: A Biology collaboration space with anatomy teaching models.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library says LIB 280 is an Anatomy Room collaboration with Biology that contains a SynDaver and muscle model.
cards.access_notes: Designed for students studying this subject area; confirm any current room-use guidance.

cards.title: Rehearse in the ScholarSpace Presentation Room
cards.subtitle: Rod Library · presentation and collaboration space
cards.notes: For a presentation-heavy group project, explore ScholarSpace’s capacity and technology details, then reserve it if the group size and schedule fit.
cards.short_summary: A library room designed for lectures, presentations, and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library describes the ScholarSpace Presentation Room as a 20–106-person lecture and collaboration space.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s reservation information; capacity and availability apply.

cards.title: Meet at Campanile Plaza
cards.subtitle: Central campus · Campanile gathering space
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a clear central meeting point, or pause to see the restored Campanile and the Sesquicentennial Bell installed there.
cards.short_summary: A renovated gathering space at UNI’s landmark Campanile.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI calls Campanile Plaza a central gathering space and says the Sesquicentennial Bell is permanently installed there.
cards.source_title: Honoring a campus icon | Our Tomorrow
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; observe any event setup or temporary access notices.

cards.title: Plan Around the Maucker Union Coffeehouse
cards.subtitle: Maucker Union · multipurpose room
cards.notes: Check the Maucker Union event schedule before gathering here, especially if your group needs the Coffeehouse’s larger presentation-style seating setup.
cards.short_summary: A named Maucker Union multipurpose space with seating for events.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI lists the Coffeehouse as a Maucker Union multipurpose room seating up to 200 lecture-style.
cards.source_title: View Space: Maucker Union | Student Involvement & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Event setup and availability are managed through Maucker Union Event Services.

cards.title: Gather in Hemisphere Lounge
cards.subtitle: Maucker Union · flexible event space
cards.notes: For a campus-group gathering, look at the Hemisphere Lounge through Event Services and confirm whether its flexible setup is available for your date.
cards.short_summary: A named flexible-setup lounge in Maucker Union.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI lists Hemisphere Lounge as a Maucker Union multipurpose room with flexible setup.
cards.source_title: View Space: Maucker Union | Student Involvement & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Check the Maucker Union event schedule and Event Services procedures before use.

cards.title: Find the Maucker Union Plaza Roof
cards.subtitle: Maucker Union · outdoor campus-ground location
cards.notes: Add the Maucker Union Plaza Roof to a daylight campus walk and check the campus-ground schedule first if you are planning a group meet-up.
cards.short_summary: A named rooftop plaza included in UNI’s campus-grounds event locations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI Event Services lists Maucker Union Plaza (Roof) among its campus grounds locations.
cards.source_title: View Space: Campus Grounds | Student Involvement & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may be affected by weather, events, or university operations.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented free UNI and Cedar Falls activities, from campus collections and gardens to public programs and outdoor music.

cards.title: Browse the UNI Gallery of Art
cards.subtitle: Kamerick Art Building, 1601 W 27th St.
cards.notes: Stop in during academic-year gallery hours to view the rotating exhibitions and permanent collection without buying a ticket.
cards.short_summary: A campus art stop with admission-free programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that all programming at the UNI Gallery of Art is admission-free.
cards.source_title: Visitor Information | College of Humanities Arts and Sciences
cards.access_notes: Open during the academic year Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed during listed academic breaks.

cards.title: Explore the UNI Museum
cards.subtitle: Rod Library, 1227 W 27th St.
cards.notes: Walk through the museum’s changing displays, then use Rod Library’s posted hours to plan a visit with friends.
cards.short_summary: Campus history, science, and cultural collections in Rod Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNI Museum states that attendance is free and that it is open whenever Rod Library is open.
cards.access_notes: Located in Rod Library and open during Rod Library hours.

cards.title: Take a botanical self-tour
cards.subtitle: UNI Botanical Center
cards.notes: Use the public self-tour window to slow down among the plant collections; check the department page before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A plant-focused campus visit open for public self-tours.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI lists the Botanical Center as free and open to the public for self-tours on most weekdays.
cards.source_title: For K12 Students | STEM Support Services
cards.access_notes: Self-tours are generally Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; some Friday afternoons are closed for maintenance.

cards.title: Watch for an observatory public program
cards.subtitle: UNI Earth & Environmental Science Department
cards.notes: Check the department’s announced public-program dates, then bring a friend for an astronomy-centered campus evening.
cards.short_summary: Public astronomy programs scheduled during the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies Observatory public programs as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: For K12 Students | STEM Support Services
cards.access_notes: Dates, times, and show information are posted by the Earth & Environmental Science Department.

cards.title: Catch a planetarium public program
cards.subtitle: UNI Earth & Environmental Science Department
cards.notes: Look up an upcoming public program and make a low-key plan around a planetarium show when one is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A free public-program option for a skyward campus outing.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies Planetarium public programs as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: For K12 Students | STEM Support Services
cards.access_notes: Check the department website for current dates, times, and show information.

cards.title: Walk the UNI Biological Preserves
cards.subtitle: UNI Campus Preserve System
cards.notes: Choose daylight for a relaxed nature walk and stay on appropriate public routes while taking in the preserve setting.
cards.short_summary: A dawn-to-dusk public nature option connected to UNI.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that its Biological Preserves are open from dawn to dusk and provide recreational opportunities for the general public.
cards.source_title: For K12 Students | STEM Support Services
cards.access_notes: Open from dawn to dusk; use daylight and follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Set up a Rod Library visitor card
cards.subtitle: Rod Library, UNI campus
cards.notes: Bring a photo ID to the Library Services Desk and ask for a visitor card for in-house databases and material checkout.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost way to use library resources during a campus visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library states it is always free and open to the public, and that visitors can obtain a free visitor card with photo ID.
cards.access_notes: Request the free visitor card at the Library Services Desk; a photo ID is required.

cards.entity_name: Cedar Falls Public Library Music Garden
cards.title: Make a few sounds in the Music Garden
cards.subtitle: Behind Cedar Falls Public Library along State Street
cards.notes: Meet behind the library and try the outdoor instruments together; keep the shared space and instruments treated with care.
cards.short_summary: Six outdoor instruments create a hands-on public music stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cedar Falls Public Library says its Music Garden is open to the public and contains six outdoor instruments.
cards.source_title: Our Music Garden | Cedar Falls Public Library
cards.access_notes: Located behind the library along State Street; follow the posted rules to respect instruments and space.

cards.entity_name: Gallagher Bluedorn Block Party at Highland Square Park
cards.title: Hear the Block Party at Highland Square
cards.subtitle: Highland Square Park, Waterloo — Aug. 14, 2026, 7–9 p.m.
cards.notes: Bring a lawn chair or blanket and join the scheduled outdoor music, food, and activity gathering without an admission charge.
cards.short_summary: A free Gallagher Bluedorn summer music stop in Waterloo.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI’s 2026 Block Party announcement lists the Highland Square Park event and says all Block Party events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Dates announced for free Gallagher Bluedorn Block Party series | inside UNI
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Aug. 14, 2026, 7–9 p.m.; the announcement encourages attendees to bring lawn chairs or blankets.

cards.entity_name: Gallagher Bluedorn Block Party at Black Hawk Park
cards.title: Plan for the Black Hawk Park Block Party
cards.subtitle: Black Hawk Park, Cedar Falls — Sept. 5, 2026, 7–9 p.m.
cards.notes: Save the scheduled Saturday evening, bring a blanket or lawn chair, and enjoy the public music-and-activities program together.
cards.short_summary: A September free outdoor music gathering in Cedar Falls.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI’s 2026 Block Party announcement lists the Black Hawk Park event and says all Block Party events are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Dates announced for free Gallagher Bluedorn Block Party series | inside UNI
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Sept. 5, 2026, 7–9 p.m.; the announcement encourages attendees to bring lawn chairs or blankets.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented UNI environments for individual work, group sessions, research, and course-specific projects.

cards.title: Rod Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • third and fourth floors
cards.notes: Reserve a room when you need a defined work session; the library describes these as individual or small-group spaces for one to six people.
cards.short_summary: A reservable room option for solo work or a small team.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library study rooms serve one to six people as individual or small-group spaces; rooms are on the third and fourth floors.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through Rod Library. One individual may reserve one study room per day for up to four hours; doors remain unlocked.

cards.title: Conference Room 272
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • main floor, north side
cards.notes: Plan a larger table-based session here: the room has six tables, 20 chairs, a wall whiteboard, and a television on a cart.
cards.short_summary: A main-floor conference room configured for a substantial group.
cards.evidence_claim: Conference Room 272 is on Rod Library's main floor north side and seats 20 with six tables, a wall whiteboard, and a 60-inch TV on a cart.
cards.access_notes: Library conference rooms are available by reservation from 5 p.m. to close Monday through Friday and on weekends during spring and fall semesters.

cards.title: ScholarSpace Room 301
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • third floor, east side
cards.notes: Use the tables, displays, projector, and presentation computer when your study group needs to rehearse or share research at room scale.
cards.short_summary: A presentation-equipped room for research sharing and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: ScholarSpace Room 301 is a third-floor venue for sharing UNI research and scholarship, with tables, displays, projection, video, and sound equipment.
cards.access_notes: The room is reservable; Rod Library directs requests needing fewer than 50 people or use outside ScholarSpace to library staff.

cards.title: Library Instruction Room 373
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • third floor, east side
cards.notes: For a tech-heavy group session, reserve this room for its six large displays, mobile whiteboards, camera, sound system, and table groups.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor instructional room with shared-display and whiteboard tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Library Instruction Room 373 has six 65-inch displays, mobile and wall-mounted whiteboards, a camera and sound system, and 12 tables.
cards.access_notes: Library instruction has priority. The space may be reserved up to one week in advance.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • main floor
cards.notes: Set up at a collaborative workstation or comfy seating area, then use nearby tutoring and research-help services to move coursework forward.
cards.short_summary: An academic commons combining work areas, technology, tutoring, and research help.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons provides collaborative workstations, group-project space, comfortable seating, technology, tutoring, and research help.
cards.access_notes: An open social academic space in Rod Library; the projection and whiteboard wall near room 218 can be reserved through the listed library contact.

cards.title: Anatomy Room LIB 280
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • main floor
cards.notes: Bring anatomy coursework and examine the SynDaver and muscle model in this Department of Biology collaboration space on the main floor.
cards.short_summary: A biology-focused room with anatomical teaching models.
cards.evidence_claim: The Anatomy Room, LIB 280, is a Rod Library and Department of Biology collaboration containing a SynDaver and a muscle model for students studying the area.
cards.access_notes: Located on Rod Library's main floor. Confirm any course-specific use expectations with the library or Department of Biology.

cards.title: Assistive Technology Study Room 315
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • third floor, south-side center
cards.notes: Use the height-adjustable table, ZoomText tools, desktop, monitor, and webcam for accessible individual or collaborative academic work.
cards.short_summary: An accessible technology room with reservable priority.
cards.evidence_claim: Assistive Technology Study Room 315 includes ZoomText tools, a networked desktop, 55-inch monitor, webcam, and motorized height-adjustable table.
cards.access_notes: Available for walk-in use by anyone; a user with a reservation has priority. Ask the Library Services Desk about disability-related assistance.

cards.title: Listening and Viewing Room 310
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • third floor near the south stairs
cards.notes: Work through assigned audio or video in this two-person room, where headphones and equipment support CDs, tapes, LPs, DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS.
cards.short_summary: A first-come room for media-based course work.
cards.evidence_claim: Listening and Viewing Room 310 accommodates up to two people and provides equipment and headphones for listening to or viewing several physical media formats.
cards.access_notes: First come, first served and not reservable; give priority to people who need the room's listening and viewing equipment.

cards.title: Mindfulness Space Room 437
cards.subtitle: Rod Library • fourth floor, northwest corner
cards.notes: Choose this named fourth-floor space when a quiet reset fits between focused work blocks; it sits beside Room 436 on the library's silent floor.
cards.short_summary: A named mindfulness room within Rod Library's silent-study floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Mindfulness Space is Room 437 in Rod Library's northwest fourth-floor corner, and the fourth floor is designated as the silent floor.
cards.access_notes: Located next to Room 436 on the fourth floor. Follow the fourth floor's silent-floor designation.

cards.title: TEACH Studio
cards.subtitle: Schindler Education Center 202
cards.notes: Use this teacher-education collaboration hub for curriculum projects that benefit from PreK–12 literature, manipulatives, technology, and shared work areas.
cards.short_summary: A Schindler-based collaboration hub for education projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The TEACH Studio in Schindler 202 provides collaborative workspaces and access to PreK–12 literature, curriculum materials, manipulatives, and technology.
cards.access_notes: Located in Schindler Education Center Room 202. Check the TEACH Studio's posted hours before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UNI customs, including living campus rituals and clearly labeled historical traditions.

cards.title: The Green Beanie Rule
cards.subtitle: Historical Iowa State Teachers College tradition
cards.notes: View the archive image and treat this as history: first-year men once wore green beanies during specified daytime hours.
cards.short_summary: A former first-year identifier, not a current student requirement.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI documents that first-year men at Iowa State Teachers College were required to wear green beanies from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; the university says current first-year students do not face these rules.

cards.title: The Green Armband Rule
cards.subtitle: Historical Iowa State Teachers College tradition
cards.notes: Use the archival account to understand this retired custom: first-year women once wore green armbands marking them as new.
cards.short_summary: A historic counterpart to the green-beanie custom.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI documents that first-year women at Iowa State Teachers College wore green armbands so others knew they were new to campus.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; not a current expectation.

cards.title: Watermelon on the First Day
cards.subtitle: Historical Orientation Week tradition
cards.notes: Look through the yearbook and newspaper images for this former opening-week gathering, traditionally held during fall Orientation Week.
cards.short_summary: A recurring early-1900s watermelon feed that connected students.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI records date the watermelon feed or feast to the early 20th century and identify Orientation Week as its traditional timing.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition that continued on and off through much of the 1900s.

cards.title: Spring at UNI, Literally
cards.subtitle: Historical 1971–1980 spring celebration
cards.notes: Explore the archived photos of SUNI Daze, a formal spring celebration with picnics, concerts, regatta races, and playful contests.
cards.short_summary: A 1970s spring festival whose name meant “Spring at UNI.”
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that SUNI Daze, meaning “Spring at UNI,” formally celebrated spring from 1971 through 1980.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; the documented formal celebration ran from 1971 to 1980.

cards.title: The Long-Running Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: Historical 1943–2000 campus holiday ceremony
cards.notes: Read the campus history before visiting the former sites near Commons and Maucker Union; the ceremony moved locations over its run.
cards.short_summary: A holiday gathering that united campus members across generations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies the Tree Lighting Ceremony as a long-standing campus holiday tradition held from 1943 to 2000.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; it is documented as having ended in 2000.

cards.title: Learn the Six-Move “Interlude”
cards.subtitle: Panther Welcome and McLeod Center tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the six-movement dance at Panther Welcome or athletics events, where UNI says new students still learn and perform it.
cards.short_summary: A UNI-created synchronized dance born in 2010.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that new students still learn the “Interlude” during Panther Welcome and that it is often done at athletics events in the McLeod Center.
cards.access_notes: Participation depends on Panther Welcome and athletics-event programming.

cards.title: Build a UNI Traditions Record
cards.subtitle: Alumni & Friends participation challenge
cards.notes: Document completed traditions with photos and follow the challenge guidance; 25 completions earn a pin and 45 earn a commencement medallion.
cards.short_summary: A continuing challenge that recognizes participation in UNI customs.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI says the Traditions Challenge continues as part of student experience and currently features 65 UNI traditions.
cards.access_notes: Review current challenge instructions and any event-specific requirements before participating.

cards.title: Ring In, Ring Out
cards.subtitle: Arrival, finals, and commencement tradition
cards.notes: Find the Sesquicentennial Bell to mark an arrival or graduation milestone; UNI also encourages rubbing it for good luck during finals.
cards.short_summary: A new bell ritual tied to the beginning and close of a UNI career.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI states that students are encouraged to ring the Sesquicentennial Bell when they arrive and around Commencement, and to rub it for finals luck.
cards.access_notes: UNI describes this as a new tradition introduced in the prior year.

cards.title: Meet Beneath the Campanile
cards.subtitle: Homecoming midnight Campanile tradition
cards.notes: If Homecoming programming includes campaniling, gather at the Campanile for the documented midnight ritual; respect event guidance and the space.
cards.short_summary: A revived Homecoming custom centered on UNI’s bell tower.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI Archives documents campaniling as kissing under the Campanile at midnight, revived for Homecoming in 1979 and part of Homecoming celebrations since.
cards.access_notes: The documented ritual is associated with Homecoming; participation is optional and event programming may vary.

cards.title: Start With Panther Welcome
cards.subtitle: Current UNI arrival tradition
cards.notes: Check the current welcome schedule when arriving on campus; UNI lists Panther Welcome among its recognized traditions and teaches the Interlude there.
cards.short_summary: A current welcome ritual that introduces new Panthers to campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI identifies Panther Welcome among today’s recognized campus traditions and states that new students learn the “Interlude” during it.
cards.access_notes: Consult current university orientation communications for dates and participation details.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Northern Iowa, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe first-weekend sequence using campus landmarks, spaces, and nearby public recreation.

cards.title: Start with the Campanile
cards.subtitle: Campus landmark walk
cards.notes: Begin with a daylight walk to the Campanile and take a few orientation photos before choosing your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable starting point for getting your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: UNI’s archives document the Campanile as a campus memorial project begun in 1914 and built after years of planning.
cards.access_notes: Visit exterior campus grounds in daylight and follow posted university access guidance.

cards.title: Settle into Rod Library
cards.subtitle: Study rooms and campus resources
cards.notes: Use the library’s space information to choose a study room or a small-group meeting room that fits your plans.
cards.short_summary: A practical pause for studying, planning, or meeting up.
cards.evidence_claim: Rod Library offers study rooms for one to six people and meeting rooms for small to medium groups.
cards.access_notes: Room availability and reservations vary; consult the library’s room-selection links before relying on a particular room.

cards.title: Find the Union’s gathering spaces
cards.subtitle: Dining, events, and social space
cards.notes: Walk through the Coffeehouse and posted event areas, then check the Union calendar or student-involvement office for options.
cards.short_summary: A central campus stop for services, food, and event information.
cards.evidence_claim: Maucker Union has a central Coffeehouse, meeting rooms, a ballroom, dining options, and hosts thousands of events annually.
cards.source_title: Welcome, Mission & History | Student Involvement & Event Services
cards.access_notes: Public areas and services vary by time and event; check the Union directly for current access.

cards.entity_name: University of Northern Iowa Gallery of Art
cards.title: Take in the Gallery of Art
cards.subtitle: Kamerick Art Building
cards.notes: Add a self-guided gallery visit during academic-year hours, and use the displayed exhibition information to slow down and look closely.

cards.evidence_claim: The UNI Gallery of Art is on the ground floor of Kamerick Art Building, and all of its programming is admission-free.

cards.access_notes: The gallery lists academic-year hours as Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with break closures; verify before visiting.
